Thesis: Gusto earns the Simple seat when applicant tracking; core hris; payroll processing; benefits admin is the weekly loop and time and attendance (Simple, Plus, Premium, Contractor Only) is unlocked; skip if Companies whose primary job is a full HRIS or people platform; High-volume recruiting / structured hiring ATS buyers; Global EOR or 1,000+ employee HCM buyers.

Best for: US small businesses running payroll (and benefits) for the first time; Teams that want published month-to-month pricing instead of HCM quotes; Single-state companies that can start on Simple and upgrade for multi-state (US small businesses running payroll (and benefits) for the first time).

Poor fit when: Companies whose primary job is a full HRIS or people platform; High-volume recruiting / structured hiring ATS buyers; Global EOR or 1,000+ employee HCM buyers. Avoid if Simple plan is single-state payroll — multi-state needs Plus would block go-live.

sections.heading: Gusto limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Simple plan is single-state payroll — multi-state needs Plus; People/HRIS depth is light versus BambooHR; Gusto is payroll-first; Time, performance, next-day pay, and many benefits tools are add-ons because it forces process changes or add-ons around Gusto when applicant tracking is the job.

Pricing interpretation: no free plan confirmed — scope a paid pilot on Simple with exit criteria before annual seats.

Plan trade-off: you gain time and attendance (Simple, Plus, Premium, Contractor Only) at the expense of Published free tiers vs paid depth for ATS, WFM, time, or training jobs — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Simple · applicant tracking | Plus | Premium.

Alternative context: unlike Rippling, Gusto is preferable when US small businesses running payroll (and benefits) for the first time because applicant tracking plus time and attendance (Simple, Plus, Premium, Contractor Only) match; prefer Rippling when Companies whose primary job is a full HRIS or people platform because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Gusto
sections.body:

Setup requires a specialist owner when Simple plan is single-state payroll — multi-state needs Plus collides with applicant tracking; SMB pilots can stay lighter if time and attendance (Simple, Plus, Premium, Contractor Only) is already on Simple.
